ci: put the shards back on ARC, run e2e under -race once, quarantine ticketed flakes (#3669)

test-unit and race-shard return to arc-runners. pkg/sandbox/kubernetes, whose Bubblewrap witnesses ARC pods refuse, leaves their partitions. The new gated leg test-native-exec proves that package plain and under -race on the CI_NATIVE_EXEC_RUNNER/VM route, behind the same fork, bot and off guards, and both test and race need it (#3662). test-e2e runs under -race with cgo and race-shard no longer packs e2e (#3664). scripts/ci/test-quarantine.tsv lists ticketed flakes (#3512, #3624, #3588). scripts/ci/testquarantine builds the -skip every gating go test applies. The nightly test-quarantine workflow runs only those tests and fails on a failure or a closed ticket (#3663). Each ciguard guard was mutation-proved.

Mutation: Every mutation was applied to production code or data, then the file was restored from a backup. sha256 before and after was identical every time (mutation harness in $TMPDIR). M1: in scripts/ci/testquarantine/main.go pattern(), `"^"+level+"$"` became `"^"+level`. TestThePatternSkipsAndSelectsExactlyTheRows went red (main_test.go:109: -skip also skipped TestFlakyButNot). M2: parse accepted a row with no ticket (`if m == nil && false`). TestParseRefusesARowACIJobCouldMisread/no_ticket went red. M3: verifyPassed ignored the depth check. TestVerifyRefusesARowWithoutItsOwnPass went red. M4: added the row `pkg/sandbox/kubernetes TestExecPreservesDriverEnvironment` to the TSV. TestTheCommittedQuarantineNamesTestsOfItsOwnPackageOnly went red: it also matches the docker and noop tests. M5: renamed a row's test. The same test went red: it names no Test function of pkg/runview. M6: removed `-skip "$quarantine"` from race-shard. TestEveryGatingGoTestSkipsTheQuarantine went red (quarantine_gate_test.go:123). M7: inlined the e2e quarantine substitution. The quarantine-exit-7 subtest went red: the step succeeded after the list was refused. M8: put test-unit back on the CI_NATIVE_EXEC_RUNNER expression (the #3662 defect). native_exec_runner_test.go:203 went red: test-unit left the scale set. M9 and M14: removed `/pkg/sandbox/kubernetes$` from the race-shard and test-unit -skip. native_exec_runner_test.go:229 went red. M10: put e2e back into race-shard's partition (the #3664 defect). e2e_shards_test.go:167 went red. M11: removed -race from the test-e2e go test. e2e_shards_test.go:134 went red. M12: removed test-native-exec from race needs. native_exec_runner_test.go:185 went red. M13: the native job's race step tested ./pkg/sandbox/docker/ instead. native_exec_runner_test.go:193 went red. Tree restored after each one; the final run is green.

Review fixes:
- The test-e2e comment now says the 1468-1785 s whole-package -race timing came from GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest (race-shard, runs 45180564490/45186345093), not ARC, and that the hash-split shards are uneven (the heaviest is about a third of the package). Each shard now keeps race-shard's proven bounds: the step goes to -timeout 2400s ./e2e and the job to timeout-minutes 50. docs/merge-policy.md (prose and reproduce command) and the ci-gate-map test-e2e residual now say 2400s.
- The native-job guard now tokenizes every `go test` line of test-native-exec. It refuses -run/-list/-short/-bench/-fuzz/-failfast in -x, --x or -x= form, and requires exactly one -skip (the quarantine's).
- Added the #3624 row for github.com/SocialGouv/iterion/pkg/runview TestAlertEpochEndRetiredQueueAndResume to scripts/ci/test-quarantine.tsv.
- pattern() now stable-sorts a clone of the entries by level count before building the alternation. Parent rows come before their subtest rows, so a parent is skipped whatever order the file lists them in. Added the slices import.
- The nightly tickets step now uses --jq 'if .pull_request then "pull-request" else .state end'. A pull-request value is a red with its own message ('is a pull request, not an issue').
- e2e discovery now runs as `pattern=$(GOFLAGS=-race go run ... testshards -tests ./e2e ...)` and keeps the inline `go test -race`, so discovery lists the same race build that execution runs. A comment says so. The merge-policy reproduce command and the ci-gate-map residual mirror it.
- Both testshards calls (test-unit and race-shard) are now anchored to the module root: -skip '^github\.com/SocialGouv/iterion/(e2e|pkg/sandbox/kubernetes)$'. The ci-gate-map test-unit residual is updated to match.
- docs/state-of-the-art.md: '`go test ./e2e/...` (900 s) + a `-race` pass' now reads '`go test -race ./e2e` in four shards (2400 s each)'. The reading golden is regenerated with go run ./cmd/corpus-reading --write.
- Moved the native-job selection tokenizer into goTestSelections(run). It now joins backslash-newline continuations before splitting and strips an optional 'test.' prefix from the flag name, so -test.run, --test.run= and a -run on a continued line all count as narrowing. TestNativeExecRunnersPreserveTrustBoundaryAndProveMounts uses the helper.
- Deleted TestTheCommittedQuarantineHoldsEveryTestItsSeedTicketsName and its comment from scripts/ci/testquarantine/main_test.go. The rows are the fix, and the nightly tickets job governs how long a row stays.

Closes #3662

fix(server): a team left with only retired forge tombstones deletes, and the tombstones go with it (#3629)

Deprovision keeps the disabled webhook config of a retired integration as an admission fence. No route removes a provisioned config, and teamResidue counted every config, so any team that ever had a forge integration answered 409 forever.

teamResidue now sets apart a disabled config bound to an integration row of the same team that is retired with its cleanup complete, or bound to a missing row. handleDeleteTeam deletes those configs and their rows (row first, so a retry converges) before the first membership revoke, and the team.deleted audit records how many. Any other hook, or a read that fails, still refuses.

Mutated: counting every hook, each of the six guards, removing the purge, the delete order, purging after the revokes, and the audit count. Each one turned its test red.

Mutation: Script $TMPDIR/qw-3250/mut.py applied 12 production mutations to pkg/server/team_lifecycle_routes.go, one at a time, ran -run 'TestTeamDelete_|TestTeamLifecycle_|TestForgeIntegration_', and restored the original text in a finally block. A grep afterwards confirmed the guarded lines are back. Red results, each on its own assertion: (1) count-every-hook ('case dead:' -> 'case dead && false:'): afterDeprovisionAndDisconnect:96 got 409 '[1 inbound webhook(s)]' instead of 204, and retiredTombstoneDeletes went red too. (2) drop the 'cfg.Enabled ||' check: hookStillRefuses/enabled got 204, want 409. (3) drop the empty-ProvisionIntegrationID check: hookStillRefuses/standalone_disabled_hook got 204. (4) drop the tenant match: hookStillRefuses/integration_of_another_team got 204. (5) drop 'ri.Retired &&': hookStillRefuses/integration_not_retired got 204. (6) drop '&& ri.RetireCleanupComplete': hookStillRefuses/retirement_cleanup_not_complete got 204. (7) treat a read error as a tombstone: hookStillRefuses/integration_store_unreadable got 204. (8) treat a missing row as live: retiredTombstoneDeletes/binding_to_a_missing_integration got 409. (9) remove the purge call: afterDeprovisionAndDisconnect:105 'tombstone survived ... err=<nil>, want webhooks.ErrNotFound' and :108 'retired integration row survived'. (10) delete the config before the row: aFailedPurgeLeavesTheTeamUntouched:302 'the tombstone went although its row could not'. (11) purge after the membership revokes: aFailedPurge:299 'a grant was revoked despite the failed purge'. (12) drop the audit count: afterDeprovisionAndDisconnect:112 'purged_webhook_tombstones = <nil>, want 1'. The 'no integration store' guard was not mutated on its own: removing it would make the purge call a method on a nil store and panic, so its test row only shows that it refuses with 409.

Review fixes:
- retiredHookTombstone guard is now `cfg.Enabled && !cfg.ProvisionFrozen || ...`. An enabled config frozen by a legacy-hook migration is now judged by its row, like a disabled one. Updated the godoc bullet, the teamResidue godoc and the docs/diagrams/flow-org-team-lifecycle.md exception sentence, and re-pinned the corpus.
- Added TestTeamDelete_aRefusedDeleteKeepsTheTombstone with two subtests. The rank refusal (403, org owner boss holds a t2 grant) and the residue refusal (409, plus a live standalone enabled hook wh2) both assert that the team, the tombstone wh1 and the retired row ri1 survive.
- Comment-only. The retiredHookTombstone godoc now says RetireCleanupComplete does not guarantee the forge-side hook is gone: Deprovision skips that deletion when the connection or admin client is unavailable, and once the tombstone is deleted those deliveries get 401 instead of 410 and launch nothing. The teamResidue godoc says 'its hook credential (a token hash, or a sealed HMAC secret)' instead of 'a sealed hook secret'.
- Added a case to TestTeamDelete_hookStillRefuses named 'frozen enabled config, retirement cleanup not complete'. It uses boundHook(true) with ProvisionFrozen=true and a row with Retired=true and RetireCleanupComplete=false, and expects 409 naming '1 inbound webhook(s)'.

Closes #3250

fix(claw): images reach vision models on OpenAI-compatible gateways (#3651)

* fix(claw): images reach vision models on OpenAI-compatible gateways

A claw node's images never reached the model on the chat-completions wire
(LiteLLM/PLIAGE): read_image, screenshot and computer_use returned their
result as JSON text, so every provider received the base64 as text, and
openaiwire and the Responses converter dropped every image block, the
prompt's {{attachments.x}} included.

- A tool registration attests an image result (imageResult, carried by
  delegate.ToolDef.ImageResult through the adapter, the sandbox runner,
  the GenerationTool conversion and subagents); shapeToolOutcome decodes
  the output into image blocks (tool.ImageResultContent), and an output
  that does not decode becomes an is_error result.
- openaiwire sends images as image_url parts (base64 as a data URL); a
  tool's images ride in the next user message, and a user message after a
  tool message is preceded by an assistant bridge: the Mistral family's
  template refuses user-after-tool. Measured on PLIAGE, tool -> assistant
  -> user is the one sequence pixtral-12b, mistral-small-3.2,
  mistral-medium-3.5, gemma-4, qwen3.5, qwen3.6 and deepseek-v4.1-flash
  all accept. An image block that cannot be encoded is refused.
- The Responses converter sends input_image parts the same way.
- Compaction's estimate counts an image block a fixed 1600 tokens.

Live proof: the reporter's vision probe bot, run locally on this build
against PLIAGE, reads the diagram correctly on all seven models (6.8-11.8k
tokens instead of ~60k of base64); glm-5.3 now fails explicitly ("not a
multimodal model") instead of inventing labels.

Mutation-checked (each restored after its witness went red): the decode
in shapeToolOutcome, the tool-image hoist and the bridge on the wire, the
flag copy in toolDefsToGeneration, the sandbox runner and subagents, and
the screenshot registration.

Refs #3642

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@example.com>

* fix(claw): close the vision change's first adversarial round

- openaiwire.Message.MarshalJSON encodes through the package's unescaped
  marshaller: json.Marshal escaped <, > and & in every chat-completions
  body (the text-only witness now goes through MarshalJSON with them).
- A tool's images wait for the end of the run of tool messages and join
  the next user message: an injected reminder or operator message no
  longer yields user, user, and tool results split across input messages
  stay contiguous after their tool_calls.
- An unencodable image block is an *api.RequestValidationError (chat and
  Responses), non-retryable like every invalid local request.
- A codemode program calling an image tool receives an explicit
  image-omitted marker instead of a bare success.
- A prompt's own image blocks keep their near-zero compaction weight; only
  a tool's images count 1600 tokens (uncatalogued gateway models compact
  at 10k and lost the task and its attachments).
- ImageResultContent refuses an image over 5 MiB of base64 (Anthropic's
  per-image cap) with an error the model recovers from by downscaling.
- The live read_image fixture asks for the colour of a solid red PNG: the
  model now receives the image, not its JSON (compiled, not run: paid).

Mutation-checked, each restored after its witness went red: json.Marshal
back in MarshalJSON; the immediate image flush; an untyped error; the
codemode image arm removed; the top-level image weight restored; the size
check disabled.

fix(claw): drop a propertyNames that admits every key from tool schemas (#3652)

An enabled MCP plugin's tools join every claw node that has tools (on
iterion.cloud with firecrawl enabled, a node declaring 8 tools sent 34).
firecrawl-mcp builds its schemas with zod v4, which writes every z.record
as "propertyNames": {"type": "string"}. claw's first agentic turn forces a
tool call (tool_choice "required"), so vLLM compiles every tool's
parameters into a grammar, and xgrammar refuses the keyword: every request
of the node failed on mistral-small-3.2 ("features not supported by
xgrammar") and qwen3.5 ("Unimplemented keys: [\"propertyNames\"]").

The shared schema cleaner drops a propertyNames that admits every key
(true, {}, a type including "string" with annotations only), at any depth:
an object key is always a string, so the meaning holds for every provider.
One that constrains keys (pattern, enum, false, a non-string type) stays.
The guarantee corpus's two null-propertyNames cases now expect {}, the
same schema.

Proof: reproduced live on the PLIAGE gateway (same two messages, only with
tool_choice "required" and the keyword; mistral-medium-3.5 tolerates it);
the real claw backend against mistral-small-3.2 with a firecrawl-shaped
tool fails with the production 500 without the change and finishes with
it. Mutation-checked: the drop disabled (vacuous keyword reaches the wire)
and the drop made unconditional (a constraining keyword is lost).

Adversarial-Rounds: 0 (small, semantics-preserving; gate review by Revi, live-proven)

fix(claw): judge capability grants on the tool surface the wire serves (#3630)

Claw's inert-grant gate counted AllowedTools, but claw builds its request's tools from ToolDefs alone. A board or runs-read grant riding AllowedTools without ToolDefs reached the model tool-less. The gate and the Tools block now call one predicate, clawServesToolDefs. The AllowedTools and interaction exemptions are gone; an interaction node passes because its ask_user is in ToolDefs. The schema re-ask stays exempt.

buildTask now logs one Warn per node execution when a prompt command's allowed-tools narrows away every tool of a board or runs-read grant.

Mutations seen red then restored: AllowedTools term re-added to the gate; clawServesToolDefs returning false; Warn removed; withAlwaysAllowed dropped; once-only claim dropped.



Mutation: Each mutant is a production edit. Every one went red on its own assertion and the file was then restored byte-identical (cmp against a saved copy; git status shows only the 5 intended files). (1) Re-added `len(task.AllowedTools) == 0 &&` to the gate in claw_backend.go: red on review_pr_converge_claw_test.go:167 'err = <nil>, want an ErrCapabilityUnsupported' (arm a_list_the_wire_never_serves_is_refused). (2) Made clawServesToolDefs `return false`: red on :177 and :190 'a served surface was refused' (declared-surface and interaction arms). (3) Removed the grant-narrowed Warn block in buildTask: red on claw_served_surface_test.go:78 and :95 'warnings = [], want one naming ...'. (4) Dropped .withAlwaysAllowed() in tool.CommandNarrowedSet: red on claw_served_surface_test.go:71 'narrowed ToolDefs = [], want exactly [todo_write]'. (5) Dropped the sess.claimWithdrawal("grant-narrowed") term: red on :81 'a second build of the same node execution warned again'.

Review fixes:
- Added the arm 'an interaction node with no ToolDefs is refused' to TestClawRefusesAnInertCapabilityGrant. The task has Capabilities [board.read], InteractionEnabled, HasTools and no ToolDefs. The arm asserts ErrCapabilityUnsupported and that no model request is spent. The doc comment's mutation list now names the mutant.
- Added the subtest 'a build that fails after the narrowing does not spend the Warn' to TestPromptNarrowingAndAClawGrant. On one nodeBuildSession, a persist node with board.read and a declared-empty narrowing first builds with input {ResumeAnswerKey:x}. That build must fail with the persisted-resume error and log no Warn. The next build succeeds and logs exactly one Warn. The doc comment's mutation list now names the mutant.
- Comment-only fix: reworded the clawServesToolDefs godoc. It now says the predicate reports whether ToolDefs is non-empty and that Execute adds codemode and memory-store tools beside ToolDefs, none of which serves a grant. It says only the gate and the Tools block read the predicate. The false 'nothing else' and 'every claw reading' claims are gone.

fix(model): judge the credential walk's provider steps on their own model (#3656)

EffectiveProviders dropped the model of each `hint:model` step, so it judged a gateway step on the node, cell or launch model next to it. A gateway step beside a vendor model widened as an unknown name, was pinned as the vendor, set CredentialPlan to nil, and was refused by an openai_compatible allowlist even though dispatch would serve it on the gateway.

chainSteps now keeps each step's model, as parseProviderChain does. chainDecides judges each step on that model, falling back to the route model, and on claw records the prefix slot of each distinct step model. A step model expanded from a `${…}` field is never treated as a raw gateway spelling.

Mutation: chainSteps dropping the step model again (`hint, _, _`) reds every origin row and the claw slot test.

Mutation: Three mutations were run on pkg/backend/model/override_fold.go. Before them the file was copied to $TMPDIR/qw-3213/orig.go, and after them it was copied back; `cmp` printed 'restored'. (1) The defect itself. In chainSteps, `hint, model, _ := ir.SplitProviderStep(token)` was changed to `hint, _, _ := ...; model := ""`. Result: exit 1, and each test failed on its own assertion: - aGatewayStep, all 3 origins: 'keyed: providers=[anthropic] narrow=false unknown=[openai_compatible]', 'sites[a]=[anthropic]', 'unkeyed: ... onlyEnvFunded=false', and the allowlist line 'refused a launch ...: provider is unreadable (names "openai_compatible")'. - aClawVendorStep, all 3 origins: 'sites[a]=[anthropic], want [anthropic zai]' and 'pins[zai]=[]'. - controls: 'env-templated field' and 'mixed chain' rows. (2) The `${…}` guard. In stepRoute, `!envStepModels &&` was changed to `(envStepModels || !envStepModels) &&`; the first try, which deleted the guard, hit a compile error instead. Result: 'env-templated field' failed with 'sites[a]=[openai_compatible], want []', 'unknown=[], want [openai_compatible]', 'narrow=true, want false'. (3) The route-model fallback. `return mdl, rawGatewayPrefix(mdl)` was changed to `return "", false`. Result: these control rows failed: 'gateway hint on the gateway route model', 'vendor hint, no step model', 'gateway hint on a vendor route model', 'mixed chain'. After restoring, the whole package is green.

Review fixes:
- chainDecides now takes a stepModels bool. When it is false, every step's model is cleared right after chainSteps, so each step is judged on the route model. resolveNode's two call sites (the provider override cell or launch var, and the node's own chain) pass true. resolveRoute (authored fallbacks: routes and run-level stages) passes false, because resolveChainUnder and call_sites fallbackSites send that field whole beside the route's model. I corrected the chainDecides godoc to say this.
- In chainDecides' claw slot-read loop, a step whose hint the allowlist forbids (len(a.allowed)>0 && !a.allowed[s.hint]) now reads no slot. This mirrors AllowlistDrops (legs.go:156), which drops a hinted step on its hint alone. A forbidden step therefore no longer marks the route inside the list. This also fixes the older model-less form. I documented it in the chainDecides godoc.

Closes #3213
